page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top. Verse in one column of full lines, with two centred titles (headings) between the verses. One marginal note at the right, beside the line "Nimirum Paulu prætulit ille Petro." Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Quæ Paulus quondam & Petrus docuere, docetq; Germani hoc nostro tempore mille uiri?
main_text.head: Huldricus Huttenus de gladio Iulij.
main_text.p: Ille sui[?] longo successor in ordine Petri, More nouo tantas res agit, & studio, Nam neq; pro populis orat, pacíq; relictus, Quod faceret Petrus, sacra fidemq; docet: Verum bella mouet, gerit arma, & sanguine gaudet[?]. Nimirum Paulu prætulit ille Petro. (det, Paulus habet gladium, sed non ferit: occidit illo. At malus hic multis intulit exitium.
main_text.head: Iulij descriptio, per eundem Huttenum.
main_text.p: Qui chalybe & duris amicitur Iulius armis, Terribilis barba, terribilisq; coma: Cui torvos horrore oculos frons occulit atrox, Tartareæ ignescunt cuius in ore minæ: Ille inquam gladijs, atq; occidente sagitta Et terra populis, & metuendus aquis: Qui trucibus reges terrarum innexuit armis, Qui tetrum excito fuit in orbe malum: Ille tot exitiorum & tanti criminis author, Quo se cum populis imminuere duces, Quiq; manu, quiq; ingenio dira omnia patrat, Natus in humanum pestis acerba genus.

page.notes: Head "Huldricus Huttenus de gladio" and "Iulij." are two lines of one title, marked as one level 2 heading. The marginal "(det," at the right of the line "Nimirum Paulu prætulit ille Petro." is a short note beside the text; its extent is unclear. The printed line "Ille sui longo" is read as "sui" with doubt. "gaudet" is cut off at the right edge of the scan and is read with doubt. The running head is "DE ROM: PONTIFICVM"; the abbreviation mark after ROM is unclear. The poem's stanza breaks are not visible, so the verse is given as one paragraph per block. The catchword "Cuius" is taken from the lower right of the page.
